sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the title and attribution for the Purim maamar of 5713.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Purim
(Maamar 2)*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the holiday is named Purim after Haman's lot, which was part of the decree, and explains that the essence of the miracle is connected to the concept of the lot itself.

translations.translation: "Therefore they called these days Purim, after the Pur [lot]."
And according to the known principle
that the name of every thing indicates its essence,
it is understood
that the reason they called these days Purim after the Pur is because the main aspect of the holiday of Purim is the lot
(Pur means the lot).
And it needs to be understood
(as is precisely noted in Torah Or, section "Zeh"),
that at first glance,
this was not
[the main aspect]
of the miracle.
Furthermore,
the lot that Haman cast
(not only was this not the miracle,
but on the contrary)
was part of the decree
[and in the language of the Megillah,
"He cast Pur, that is the lot, to destroy them and to annihilate them"],
and from the fact that these days are called Purim after the Pur,
it implies that this
(the lot)
is the main aspect of the miracle of Purim,
to the extent that the miracle is named after it.
And at first glance, it could be explained according to what is stated in the Gemara,
that when the lot fell in the month of Adar, [Haman] rejoiced
(Haman)
with great joy,
saying, "A lot has fallen for me in the month in which Moshe died,"
and he did not know that on the seventh of Adar he died and on the seventh of Adar he was born.
And based on this, it could be said
that the reason these days are called after the Pur is because the miracle of Purim was that the lot fell in the month of Adar,
the month in which Moshe, the savior of Israel, was born.
But this explanation is still difficult,
because from the fact that the holiday is called Purim after the Pur,
it implies
that the connection of the miracle to the Pur is
(not only to the fact that the lot fell in the month of Adar,
but also)
to the matter of the Pur itself.
And on the contrary,
the main aspect of the miracle was from the aspect of the Pur, which is the lot.
For a lot is a very exalted matter,
from which the miracle is drawn.
And that the lot fell on the month of Adar, in which the savior of Israel was born, is
(like all the matters that occurred in the miracle of Purim,
which are)
a result of its main essence,
Purim after the Pur.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection between Purim and Yom Kippur, noting that both involve the concept of a lot and are above the level of the name Havayah.

translations.translation: B)
And this will be understood according to what is explained in Torah Or,
that Purim and Yom HaKippurim are related to each other.
For the explanation of Yom K.
Purim is like Purim
[and moreover,
from the fact that Yom HaKippurim is K.
Purim
(with only the comparative letter Kaf),
it is proven
that Purim is more elevated than Yom HaKippurim].
And the connection between Yom HaKippurim and Purim is
that in both there is the matter of the lot.
For on Yom HaKippurim they cast a lot upon the two goats,
and also Purim is named after the Pur, which is the lot.
And another matter in the connection of Purim and Yom HaKippurim,
that both are above the level of the name Havayah.
For regarding Yom HaKippurim it is written,
"Before Havayah you shall be purified,"
[meaning] above Havayah.
And also regarding Purim it is known
that the reason the name Havayah is not mentioned in the entire Megillat Esther
is because on Purim there is a revelation of the Ein Sof that is above Havayah.
